check_service_status.description: Check whether Islamic Network is answering, and how quickly. This is five separate services on five hosts, so each is checked and reported on its own: 'ok' is true only when all five answered. Put this in front of a long workflow and branch on it, rather than discovering one service is down halfway through. Never fails the step. No API key required.
check_service_status.display_str_template: Check the Islamic Network service status.
check_service_status.name: check_service_status

find_person.description: Find a prophet, saint, scholar or companion by name and get back the slug the other steps need. The step to put in front of the rest when all a workflow has is a name out of a form field. Diacritics are folded by the service, so 'ali' finds the names written with their marks. No API key required.

get_todays_devotions.description: What to read today: the day's name, what is traditionally done on it, and the prayers, salawaat, adhkaar and duas offered. Most days of the year are ordinary days, so this usually comes back with 'has_devotions' false and a 'next' pointing at the coming blessed day, with the days until it where that can be counted. Branch on 'has_devotions' to stay quiet on an ordinary morning, or announce what is coming. No API key required.
get_todays_devotions.name: get_todays_devotions

parameters.description: The Gregorian day to resolve, as YYYY-MM-DD. Leave empty for today. Islamic Network's own routes insist on DD-MM-YYYY and answer anything else with an error, so either spelling is accepted here and converted on the way out: a date picker's value can be passed straight in.
parameters.name: date

get_todays_events.description: What happened on today's Hijri date. Like the devotional calendar, most days carry nothing, so this usually returns 'has_events' false with a 'next' pointing at the coming anniversary. Branch on 'has_events' rather than posting an empty list. No API key required.
